Fixture: don't re-open a hidden OneTrust surface that already holds the user's choice

Modelled on measurements taken from the real www.cnbc.com on 2026-09-06 (Playwright, real unpacked extension, reject_all): after the first page answered the CCPA opt-out, every subsequent page load still produced a fresh cmp_api:OneTrust:ccpa action — 3 recorded actions across 3 page views — even though OptanonConsent already carried OSSTA_BG:0 at t=0 of each load and OptanonAlertBoxClosed was present the whole time.

The measured page shape is reproduced exactly, because it is what makes the bug possible:

  • NO #onetrust-banner-sdk in the DOM at all — the site is not asking.
  • #onetrust-pc-sdk present but display:none (0x0) — a hidden surface the extension opens itself, rather than one the site put up.
  • A persistent footer "Your Privacy Choices" opener, always in the DOM.
  • ot-group-id-OSSTA_BG already reflecting the saved opt-out.

So the first page view must act (nothing is recorded yet), and every page view after it must do nothing at all: no opened preference center, no save, no reported action, no additional "cookie eaten". Opening a modal on every page to re-apply a choice that is already saved is the exact behaviour reported live: "cnbc is still showing the modal and getting dismissed on every page they have".
